title: Source-grounded temporary support modifier states
objective: Continue Roadmap Step 6 by implementing the eight source-declared temporary attack/defense/speed/luck increase/decrease states and an AssistMagic resolver for first-party single/all targets.
evidence: Pinned CombatEnums.cs defines ActorCombatStateType AttackIncrease/Decrease, DefenseIncrease/Decrease, LuckIncrease/Decrease and SpeedIncrease/Decrease with comments stating temporary +/-10%.
Pinned SkillInfo schema carries CombatStateImpactTypes and target/resource fields, so support state changes can remain in the existing SkillDefinition combat-state effect contract.
hypothesis: The verified target/resource transaction architecture can support these eight temporary modifier states without inventing duration or stat rounding by storing state presence, exposing exact +/-10% metadata, and emitting typed combat-state change facts.
design_constraints: Use only AssistMagic with FirstPartySingle or FirstPartyAll in this slice.
Support exactly one combat-state effect per skill.
Support only the eight upstream attack/defense/speed/luck increase/decrease states.
Expose source-grounded +/-10 percent metadata without applying an invented integer rounding policy to Attack/Defense yet.
Reject duplicate application, removal of missing states and opposite-state conflicts before MP mutation rather than invent refresh/cancel semantics.
Spend MP once only after target identity/state/resource preconditions pass.
Preserve target order from CombatTargetResolver<TKey> and reject aliased target states.
Emit one SkillCast fact plus one typed CombatStateChanged fact per target.
Do not implement duration, rounds, stacking, refresh, cancellation, turn scheduler, Unity VFX or original stat rounding.
claim_boundary: This experiment models only source-declared temporary +/-10% support-state presence, first-party targeting, MP transaction and typed state-change facts. It does not establish original PAL3 duration, stacking, refresh/cancellation, effective integer stat rounding, real GDB population frequency, Unity compile/runtime, iOS or playtest behavior.
next_if_pass: Inspect original data/runtime evidence for modifier duration/rounding before consuming support percentages in normal-attack or scheduler math; otherwise proceed to another source-grounded support sub-slice.
